A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpeechMedAssist and provide readable main text, appendices, equations, tables, and figures. Material can be matched reliably across the section moves and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, training ablations, noise and cough tests, and voting by medical professionals, including Tables 2–9 and Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds vocal-signal recognition results and alternative ASR/TTS comparisons in Tables 10–11.

M1.justification: The architecture, text-based knowledge injection, and second-stage modality re-alignment remain unchanged. Appendix F extends the existing approach to additional vocal signals without specifying a new algorithm component, architecture, or objective.

E1.justification: v2 introduces VocalSound and a five-category vocal-recognition evaluation, extending v1's cough-focused testing to sighs, sneezes, sniffs, and throat clearing. This adds a distinct recognition task and represented vocal data; the existing medical and general-knowledge benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Table 11 adds eight cascaded comparator variants: FunASR-Nano or MultiMedWhisper with CosyVoice3 around Zhongjing, DISC-MedLLM, HuatuoGPT2, and Baichuan2. These augment the earlier SenseVoiceSmall/CosyVoice2 comparisons. Separately, v2 removes the Baichuan-7B comparator from the text-based AIHospital comparison in Table 9.

E3.justification: Table 10 adds per-category recognition accuracy with 598 or 599 evaluation examples per category. Table 11 introduces ASR/TTS configuration comparisons using retained Ency, MedSafety, and AIHospital metrics. Existing experimental protocols are not revised, and the new vocal experiment's training and split details remain sparse.

E4.justification: New Appendices F–G test generalization beyond cough and whether alternative ASR/TTS components narrow cascaded systems' performance gap. These add substantive generalization and component-sensitivity analyses. The existing OpenS2S and alternative-judge analyses are relocated unchanged to Sections 5.6–5.7.

E5.justification: Figure 5 retains the same variance reporting at training steps 5k and 97k. No new seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests appear. Table 10's correct/total counts describe evaluation samples rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 10 adds recognition accuracies of 90.15–94.15%, and Table 11 adds eight pipeline result sets, including HuatuoGPT2/FunASR-Nano/CosyVoice3's Ency score of 65.39. These are results under additional settings, not same-setting gains over v1. Table 9 removes Baichuan-7B's results, including its 7.12 average; other matched results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The architecture definitions and Section 3.2 domain-adaptation bound, assumptions, and accompanying mathematical reasoning are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same core contributions: SpeechMedAssist, its two-stage training strategy, the data-construction pipeline, and SpeechMedBench. The claim that approximately 10k speech samples suffice for re-alignment is unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendices F–G add interpretations concerning generalization to broader vocal cues and persistence of safety and diagnostic advantages with alternative ASR/TTS systems. Ethical Considerations newly restricts use to professional supervision. The existing Mandarin and modality limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The first-page repository description changes from 'Code&Audio Samples' to 'Code & Data & Weight,' newly advertising dataset and model-weight access through the same link. v2 also identifies CFFF as a partial computational-resource provider. Actual repository contents cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Fun-ASR, CosyVoice 3, VocalSound, and MultiMed, supporting the additional experiments. The existing related-work discussion and central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Appendices B–C become Sections 5.6–5.7, subsequent appendices are renumbered, and new Appendices F–G and an acknowledgment are inserted. Small terminology, capitalization, and cross-reference edits accompany this localized reorganization; most existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 10–11, moves Table 6 and Figure 6 into the main text, removes one row from Table 9, and adjusts surrounding table placement. Figure 2 corrects the knowledge-injection label and changes 'Modality Alignment' to 'Modality Re-Alignment.' Existing plots retain their data and design.

improvement.justification: The new vocal-signal tests broaden evidence beyond cough, while Table 11 tests whether the medical advantages persist with alternative speech-processing components. Moving existing verification into the main text and specifying professional supervision also improve clarity. These gains are limited by sparse training/split documentation for the vocal experiment and the unexplained loss of one Table 9 comparator. The core method and principal results remain unchanged.
